verdicts.evidence: The if comparison calls os.environ.get("BUILD_EXTENSION") as its test, so the cited site tests the named API. (s1)
The if test compares the result of os.environ.get("BUILD_EXTENSION") with the string "no" using ==; this is the positive condition for the then branch. (s1, s2)
The condition reads BUILD_EXTENSION from os.environ, so env_var is the correct category. (s1)

The single if condition controls the then assignment and its else alternative, with no additional guard or condition; the expression is c1 and the minimum condition count is one on either side. (s2, s3, s4)

When BUILD_EXTENSION is not "no", the else branch supplies an Extension object in ext_modules, enabling the speedups extension to be included in the setup configuration; the no branch disables it. (s2, s3, s4)
The environment variable selects whether the optional speedups extension is included; the code does not inspect analysis, CI, or sandbox conditions or back off from them, so activate fits. (s1, s2)

The comments say the extension is built only if possible when the variable is unset, and mark the extension optional unless explicitly forced with "yes"; this makes the gate's purpose portability rather than unclear. (f1:20-21, s2)
The Extension constructor call is directly inside the else branch controlled by the cited if, and s4 is that branch region. (s2, s4, s5)

The Extension constructor call appears only in the else branch; the full setup.py also shows no other call site for this constructor or route that reaches this same sink outside the gate. (s4, s5, f1:1-39)

The cited setuptools.Extension call constructs an extension configuration object; the build is delegated later to setuptools.setup, so this constructor itself is not a sink that performs the benign build. (s5, f1:34-39)
